agenda_text:
This meeting will be held via teleconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19
and pursuant to AB361. All votes taken during this teleconference meeting will be by roll call vote,
and the vote will be publicly reported.

HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may observe
the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. The meeting will be live streamed at
https://malibucity.org/video and https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to submit
email correspondence to kriesgo@malibucity.org before the meeting begins.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: Members of the public may also speak during
the meeting through the Zoom application. The City requests that you sign up to speak before the item you
would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the Zoom conference
to be recognized.

Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing up to speak and
downloading the Zoom application.

  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

As a result of the Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, the City is under a state of local emergency. In order
to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19, the Commission meeting will be open and public but conducted
 Parks and Recreation Commission Special Meeting Agenda  Page 3 of 3  December 12, 2023

virtually because meeting in person would present imminent risks to the health or safety of attendees. This
way the public, the staff, and the Commission will not be physically in the same place.

The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which are not listed on the agenda
but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no action may be taken, the Commission and staff will
follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items needing response. Each speaker is limited to (3) three minutes. Members of the
public wishing to speak during the meeting must participate through the Zoom application. The City requests that you sign up to
speak before the item you would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the Zoom
conference to be recognized. Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing up to speak
and downloading the Zoom application.

Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous meeting where the public
was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not subject to public discussion at this meeting because
the vote taken at the previous meeting was final. Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous meetings are for the purpose
of memorializing the decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any conditions imposed.

Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If discussion is desired, an item
may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual consideration. Commissioners may indicate a negative or abstaining
vote on any individual item by so declaring prior to the vote on the motion to adopt the entire Consent Calendar. Items excluded
from the Consent Calendar will be taken up by the Commission following the action on the Consent Calendar. The Commission
first will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been submitted. Public speakers shall follow the rules as set
forth under Oral Communication.

Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this meeting with no final
action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.

Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public comment shall follow the rules
as set forth under Oral Communication.

Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described above are on file in the
office of the City Manager, and available upon request by emailing kriesgo@malibucity.org.

The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device for the deaf (TDD),
please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In compliance with the Americans with
Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please contact Environmental Sustainability
Director Yolanda Bundy, (310) 456-2489, ext. 229. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make
reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. [28 CFR 35.102-35.104 ADD Title II]. Requests for use of audio
or video equipment during a Commission meeting should be directed to media@malibucity.org before 12:00 p.m. on the day of
the meeting.

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury, under the laws of the State of California, that the foregoing agenda was posted in
accordance with the applicable legal requirements. Dated this 8th day of December 2023, at 10:00 a.m.

  _____________________________________
  Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director

Subject:  Community Services Department Monthly Report

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive and file a report of activities, events, projects, and
programs coordinated by the Community Services Department in October and November
2023.

DISCUSSION: The Community Services Department coordinated the following activities,
projects, and programs in October and November 2023.

OCTOBER: RECREATION

Aquatics: Aquatics staff attended an in-service training on October 28. Training topics
included hypothermia awareness and treatment, cardiac arrest signs and symptoms, and
in-water rescue skills for passive and active drowning. Katherine Mutchler, a certified Red
Cross Lifeguard Instructor, instructed the training.

Community Classes: The fall session of Aspects Surf Academy concluded on October 6
with ten participants. The Department reformatted the popular summer day camp to a
weekly surfing class at Surfrider Beach, Tower 3, from September to October.

Fall afterschool programs and community classes continued through October,
including adult barre fitness, all sorts of sports, ballet, cheerleading, hip-hop
dance, LEGO® engineering, and soccer.

Seniors: Weekly senior recreation programs include art, ballet, cardio salsa, chair yoga,
choir, knitting, mat yoga, Pilates, relax through coloring, stretch and strength, and tap/jazz
dance combination class. Programs occur at the Senior Center and Malibu Bluffs Park.

On October 11, recreation staff led a pumpkin painting activity at the Senior Center. Staff
provided Halloween-themed accessories to make pumpkins into witches, bats, and
ghosts. Refreshments were served during the activity.
  Page 1 of 5  Agenda Item # 2.B.1.
 On October 17, eighteen seniors attended the Los Angeles Zoo excursion. Attendees
observed different species of animals and explored the grounds. Participants enjoyed
lunch at the various cafes throughout the property.

The Senior Resource Fair took place on October 19 at the Senior Center. Eighteen local
service providers and organizations, including medical doctors, health and wellness
businesses, community organizations, and senior care providers, were onsite with
informational booths. The raffle included giveaway baskets from each vendor, and pre-
registered participants had a complimentary boxed lunch from Subway.

The "Malibu Monster Mash" luncheon occurred on October 26 with 72 participants.
Bubbleoligist Megan McIver provided entertainment and created human-sized bubbles.
Recreation staff raffled four prize bags and handed out Dial-A-Ride sponsored giveaways.

Participants walked the trails at Malibu Bluffs Park and learned about native plants and
habitats during the Halloween Hike on October 31.

Social Media: Community programs, Halloween events, Malibu arts programs, and senior
center programs were featured in the Department's October social media. Analytics
indicate 2,512 followers, with 15% of Malibu residents in the 90264 and 90265 zip codes.

Special Events: Park Tales "Costume Countdown" took place at Malibu Bluffs Park on
October 5. Twenty-five families participated in a Storytime event and pirate treasure hunt.
Registered families also received a giveaway bag with city program flyers, snacks,
stickers, and an art activity supplied by the Malibu Library.

The Halloween CineMalibu movie in the park event was held on October 13 at Malibu
Bluffs Park with a screening of "The Addams Family" for 100 participants. Event highlights
included movie trivia hosted by the Harry Barovsky Memorial Youth Commission and a
mobile D'Amore's Pizza food truck.

The Halloween Bu-Bash Carnival was held on October 27 at Malibu Bluffs Park for over
200 participants. Children ages ten and under enjoyed Halloween-themed carnival games
and activities. Event highlights included bounce houses, food trucks, a costume catwalk,
and an art activity with the Malibu Library.

Sports: Player evaluations for the youth and middle school winter basketball leagues
(grades 4 through 8) were held on October 25 and 28 in the small gymnasium of Malibu
High School. Seventy-five registered participants attended the evaluations to create
balanced teams for the season.

OCTOBER: PARK MAINTENANCE

Equestrian Park: Removed graffiti from the interior men's bathroom, and residual graffiti
marks were covered with matching paint.
  Page 2 of 5  Agenda Item # 2.B.1.
 Legacy Park: On October 2, Managed Career Solutions crew began removing nonnative,
invasive plants in the leach field and cleared approximately one acre of mustard,
euphorbia, and castor bean. The crew also thinned about one acre of coastal golden bush
in preparation for the winter planting in the central part of the park.

Unclogged drinking fountain drains using a cable snake. Replaced concrete drain boxes
with metal grate lids and 18-inch valve boxes with solid lids. The new valve boxes will
prevent debris from entering the drain outlet.

Malibu Bluffs Park: Staff removed and replaced broken bleacher planks from one bleacher
set to another. The extra bleacher pieces were salvaged and will be used as spare parts
for future repairs.

Staff took an inventory of park supplies and ordered new supplies for the season.
Restocked supplies included pet waste bags for the dispensers located throughout the
park system and restroom supplies such as soap and toilet seat covers.

Trancas Canyon Park: Met with Deputies from Lost Hills Sheriff's Department to obtain a
police report regarding vandalism to the multipurpose field turf. The offender cut the lock
and chain to the entrance gate and drove a vehicle to the newly renovated turf.

NOVEMBER: RECREATION

Aquatics: The winter session of the Malibu Aquatics Foundation Seawolves swim team
and adult masters conditioning program began on November 27. Thirty-two participants
registered for the swim team, and nine adults registered for the adult masters conditioning
program.

Fall youth water polo, instructed by the Los Angeles Water Polo Club, concluded on
November 20. Thirty-three participants, ages 10 through 14, participated in the practice-
based program.

Community Classes: Fall afterschool programs and community classes, including ballet,
hip hop, cheerleading and dance, tai chi, and skateboarding, continued through
November.

Seniors: Weekly senior recreation programs continued at the Senior Center and Malibu
Bluffs Park. Existing programs include art, ballet, cardio salsa, chair yoga, choir, knitting,
mat yoga, Pilates, relax through coloring, stretch and strength, and tap/jazz dance combo.

Technology help sessions for eight seniors occurred on November 14 and 28. Staff
assisted participants with questions regarding their smartphones, tablets, and laptops.

Theater Thursday at the Malibu Senior Center took place on November 16 with nine
participants. Attendees watched "The Bucket List" and enjoyed complimentary popcorn.
  Page 3 of 5  Agenda Item # 2.B.1.
 The "Golden Days of Fall" luncheon occurred on November 30 with 78 participants. Lunch
included chicken caprese sandwiches, avocado salad, and pasta salad. Elvis
impersonator James Kruk provided entertainment, and four attendees received raffle
prizes. The dessert consisted of Porto's pastries provided by 1Heart Caregiver Services.

Social Media: November social media featured community programs, winter program
registration, arts programs, and senior programs. The Department gained ten new
followers on Instagram.

Special Events: Park Tales, "A' is for Apple," took place at Malibu Bluffs Park on November
2. Seven families participated in a Storytime event and received a giveaway bag with city
program flyers, snacks, stickers, and an art activity supplied by the Malibu Library.

Sports: On November 9 and 16, youth and middle school basketball coaches' meetings
and team drafts occurred at Malibu City Hall. Staff provided game schedules, rosters,
rulebooks, uniforms, and other helpful league information. One hundred twenty-two
participants registered for the kindergarten through eighth-grade league. Games begin
December 1 and 2 at Malibu High School.

Adult softball league playoffs took place on November 12 at Malibu Bluffs Park. Teams
participated in a single-elimination playoff en route to the championship game. "Pitches
Be Crazy" won the Championship game.

Youth tennis, instructed by John Rom, concluded on November 18 with eight participants.
Classes took place on Saturdays at the Malibu High School tennis courts.

NOVEMBER: PARK MAINTENANCE

Charmlee Park: Wattles were placed throughout the park in areas susceptible to erosion
from winter weather.

Equestrian Park: A graffiti solvent was used to remove graffiti inside the men's restroom
and staff covered graffiti on the pipe chase door using matching paint.

Wattles were placed throughout the park in areas susceptible to erosion from winter
weather.

Las Flores Park: Removed a downed park sign and damaged four-foot by six-foot wood
support posts. Purchased two replacement posts, mounting hardware, and covered posts
with two coats of paint. The sign will be assembled and installed during the first week of
December.

Wattles were placed throughout the park in areas susceptible to erosion from winter
weather. Additional storm preparation included cleaning debris from v-ditches and drains.

  Page 4 of 5  Agenda Item # 2.B.1.
 Legacy Park: Installed one breakaway anchor and one twelve-foot-tall steel signpost with
for the "City Hall" directional sign on the northeast corner of Civic Center Way and Web
Way.

Wattles were placed throughout the park in areas susceptible to erosion from winter
weather.

Worked with LA County Department of Agriculture to remove 50% of the Scirpoides
Holoschoenus (bulrush) from the detention basin and surrounding basin drains. Additional
maintenance included removing dirt and debris from the forebay, which was designed to
catch eroding debris through the city's drainage system. The debris is removed and
disposed of off-site at a landfill each year.

Pruned all Muhlenbergia Rigens (deer grass).

Malibu Bluffs Park: Installed six "No Overnight Parking" signs along the perimeter of the
dirt parking lot near the Temporary Skatepark.

Acquired proposals for roof repairs. Met multiple roofing contractors on site to provide
estimates for tarping, repairing, and replacing the roof of the Michael Landon Center.

Installed wood stakes to support newly planted shrubs in the skate park parking lot. The
shrubs were damaged due to high winds.

Repaired a three-inch irrigation backflow device.

Removed a raptor perch damaged during high winds and prepared the area for a new
perch.

Medians and Parkways: Commenced repairs on an irrigation line in the parkway planter
on Cross Creek Road.

Michael Landon Center: Replaced two diaphragms in the exterior women's restroom
closets.

Relocated the charging station and janitor cleaning cart to an accessible and convenient
location in the storage room.

Trancas Canyon Park: Wattles were placed throughout the park in areas susceptible to
erosion from winter weather.

ATTACHMENTS: None.

Subject:  Parks and Recreation Commission Rules of Procedure and
  Decorum

RECOMMENDED ACTION: 1) Review the Parks and Recreation Commission Rules of
Procedure and Decorum; and 2) Recommend revisions for adoption by Resolution at
the next Commission Regular meeting.

DISCUSSION: On August 20, 2019, The Commission adopted Resolution No. PRC
19-01, amending its Rules of Procedure and Decorum for the Conduct of Parks and
Recreation Commission Regular meetings, including Section 4.C., which reads as
follows:

Regular Meeting Schedule
  The Commission shall hold their regular meetings on the third Tuesday of every
  month, starting promptly at 5:30 p.m. The Commission shall not hear any new
  items of business after 9:00 p.m. unless a majority of the Commission votes to
  suspend the rules to do so.

Section 2.32.070 of the Malibu Municipal Code requires that the meeting schedule for
the Commission meetings be adopted by Resolution.

At the October 17, 2023 Regular meeting, the Commission requested staff to bring
back an item to change the meeting start time to a later time due to the expiration of
AB361 and meetings returning in-person, rather than on the Zoom platform.

The Commission may review the Rules of Procedure and Decorum and provide
revision recommendations, including the meeting time change. If approved, any
revisions to the Bylaws would be adopted by Resolution of the Parks and Recreation
Commission at the next Regular meeting.

Subject:  Malibu Bluffs Park Vehicle Barriers

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Review and provide feedback regarding the design and
type of vehicle barriers for Malibu Bluffs Park.

DISCUSSION: Winter Mesa Drive is the sole vehicle entrance to Malibu Bluffs Park.
The road approaches a “T” intersection for vehicles to turn right (west) into the main
parking lot, which services the Michael Landon Center, or left (east) to the Major
Baseball Field and Temporary Skatepark. As vehicles approach the intersection, they
are at a 90-degree angle, perpendicular to the Pony Field bleachers on the first base
side. This area also includes no-stopping and loading zones (Attachment 1).

In recent years, solo vehicle accidents have occurred at the Malibu Bluffs Park entrance,
typically between midnight and 4:00 AM. Drivers do not complete the right or left turn at
the intersection, resulting in a collision with the bleachers. Since 2015, the Department
has replaced the bleachers three times due to accidents. This year, on June 16, the
Department of California Highway Patrol filed a traffic crash report. Following the
accident, the City replaced one set of bleachers, two concrete support posts, and
spectator netting.

As a park safety measure, staff proposes installing barriers in the area to prevent vehicle
access from entering the baseball spectator area. Staff have worked with the City Public
Works and Planning Departments to obtain information on vehicle barriers. Several
types of barriers could be installed at the end of the “T” intersection (Attachment 2).

  Page 1 of 2  Agenda Item # 4.B.
 The Commission may discuss and provide recommendations regarding the design of the
Malibu Bluffs Park barriers, which will be placed adjacent to the Malibu Bluffs Park Pony
Field bleachers.
